titulo.en: I arrived in Quito two months ago

objetivo.en: Tell what you did with -ar verbs, say when it happened (yesterday, last Saturday, ago) and since when you have lived somewhere.

nota.en: Pasado means “last”: la semana pasada = last week.
hace + amount of time: hace dos meses = two months ago.
desde + a starting point: desde septiembre = since September.

traduccion.en: to go for a walk, to stroll

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Llegé a Quito hace dos meses.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Llegué a Quito hace dos meses.

explicacion.en: With verbs in -gar, the yo form of the preterite is spelled gu: llegué. Without the u, ge would sound like “heh”, not like the g in go.
Use desde with a starting point (desde septiembre) and hace with an amount of time (hace dos meses).
Ayer talks about a finished past action, so the verb needs the preterite: visité, not the present visito.
The tilde matters: hablé (I spoke) is stressed on the last syllable. Without it, hable is a different form.

titulo.en: Sound of the day: gu and qu in the preterite

texto.en: To keep the hard sound of g and k, Spanish changes the spelling in the yo form of the preterite. Before e or i, the letter g sounds like a strong English “h” (gente) and c sounds like “s”, so llegar becomes llegué (with gu) and buscar becomes busqué (with qu). The u is silent: gue sounds like “geh” (g as in go) and que sounds like “keh”. Say them slowly: llegué, busqué, toqué. The tilde on the é shows the stress: ye-GEH.

titulo.en: The preterite of -ar verbs

texto.en: The preterite tells what you did and finished: Ayer visité el museo. Drop -ar and add the endings: -é (yo), -aste (tú), -ó (él, ella, usted), -amos (nosotros), -aron (ustedes, ellos, ellas). With hablar: hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablaron. The tilde on -é and -ó marks the stressed last syllable and changes the meaning: hablo = I speak (now), habló = he or she spoke. With nosotros, -ar verbs look the same in the present and the preterite (hablamos); the time word tells you which one it is: ayer hablamos = we spoke yesterday. Ustedes uses the same form as ellos: ustedes hablaron.

titulo.en: When it happened: ayer, hace and desde

texto.en: Time words that go with the preterite: ayer (yesterday), anoche (last night), el sábado pasado (last Saturday), la semana pasada (last week). Hace + an amount of time means “ago”: Llegué a Quito hace dos meses = I arrived in Quito two months ago. It can also go first: Hace dos meses llegué a Quito. To say since when something has been true, use desde + a date with the present tense: Vivo en Quito desde septiembre. English says “I have lived”; Spanish uses the present because you still live there. Ask ¿Desde cuándo vives aquí? Do not use hace for “since”.

titulo.en: I ate, I went out and I wrote

objetivo.en: Tell what you ate, drank or wrote, and what time you went out and came back, with the preterite of -er and -ir verbs.

traduccion.en: to go up, to get on (a bus)

explicacion.en: -er and -ir verbs use -í in the yo form of the preterite. The ending -é belongs to -ar verbs (hablé).
Ayer talks about a finished past action, so use the preterite: comí, not the present como.
Salí is yo. With Daniela (she), use salió. Both have a tilde, on the last syllable.
Without the tilde the stress moves to the wrong syllable. Volví is stressed on the last one: vol-VÍ.

titulo.en: Sound of the day: b and v

texto.en: In Spanish, b and v sound exactly the same. Never put your teeth on your lip for v as in English: both letters sound like a b. At the beginning of a phrase, or after m or n, it is a firm b (bien, vamos). Between vowels it is softer: the lips almost touch without closing. Say them slowly: bebí, escribí, volví, viví. The first sound of bebí and volví is the same.

titulo.en: The preterite of -er and -ir verbs

texto.en: To tell what you did and finished with -er and -ir verbs, drop the ending and add: -í (yo), -iste (tú), -ió (él, ella, usted), -imos (nosotros), -ieron (ustedes, ellos, ellas). The endings are the same for -er and -ir: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comieron; escribí, escribiste, escribió, escribimos, escribieron. The tilde on -í and -ió marks the last syllable: comí = I ate, comió = he or she ate. Do not mix them up with -ar verbs: hablé, but comí. Useful verbs: comer, beber, escribir, salir, volver, recibir, compartir, subir, decidir. To ask: ¿Qué comiste el sábado? To answer: Comí una empanada y un helado.

titulo.en: I went to the Mitad del Mundo

objetivo.en: Tell where you went, what you did and how it was, with fui, fuiste, fue and hice, hiciste, hizo.

nota.en: No tilde: ui is one syllable.
No tilde: ue is one syllable.

explicacion.en: Hacer is irregular in the preterite: the yo form is hice, not hací. The endings of regular -er verbs do not apply.
Hizo is spelled with z: before o, the letter c would sound like a k, so Spanish writes z to keep the s sound.
Ayer needs the preterite: fui, not the present voy.
Fui is only for yo. For the trip, a third person, use fue.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Fuí a la Mitad del Mundo.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Fui a la Mitad del Mundo.

explicacion.en: Fui has no tilde. Unlike comí or salí, ui is one syllable, so there is no stress mark.

titulo.en: Sound of the day: diphthongs ui and ue

texto.en: In fui, fue and fueron, two vowels share one syllable. The u here sounds like an English “w”: fui is “fwee”, fue is “fweh”, fueron is “FWEH-rohn”. Because each is a single syllable, fui and fue have no tilde (not “fuí”). Say them slowly: fui, fue, fuimos, fueron.

titulo.en: Fui and hice: two irregular preterites

texto.en: Ir (to go) has its own preterite: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fueron. Ser (to be) has exactly the same forms, and the context tells you which verb it is: Fui a la Mitad del Mundo = I went; El viaje fue muy divertido = The trip was very fun. Hacer (to do, to make) has hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicieron. Note hizo is written with z. None of these forms has a tilde. To ask: ¿Qué hiciste el sábado? ¿A dónde fuiste el domingo? To answer: Fui a la Mitad del Mundo. Hice una excursión con Daniela. To give an opinion, use fue + adjective: El viaje fue muy divertido. El museo fue interesante.

titulo.en: Level review: my day, my likes and my neighborhood

objetivo.en: Review the essentials of A1: tell the time of your routine, your likes, where something is and what you buy at the market.

traduccion.en: they please: me gustan = I like (several things)
it delights: me encanta = I love
they delight: me encantan = I love (several things)

explicacion.en: The verb agrees with the thing you like, not with yo: one thing = me gusta, several things = me gustan.
Gustar works backwards: dancing pleases me. Say me gusta, never yo gusto.
For one o'clock, use the singular: es la una. From two on, use son las: son las dos.
Cerca needs de: cerca de la plaza, and cerca del parque (de + el = del).

erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Una libra de tomates, por favor.

explicacion.en: Quantities are followed by de: una libra de tomates, medio kilo de queso.

titulo.en: Sound of the day: r and rr

texto.en: The letter r is called erre. Between vowels, a single r is one quick tap of the tongue, like the tt in American “butter”: pero, caro, para. At the beginning of a word, and in rr, the tongue vibrates: rico, carro, perro, arroz. The difference changes the meaning: pero means “but” and perro means “dog”. Before a consonant, as in cerca, the r is a light tap. Say them slowly: arroz, carro, perro, cerca, rico.

titulo.en: What you can already say at A1

texto.en: This class reviews four things you have learned. 1) The time and your routine: Son las ocho menos cuarto. Me levanto a las seis y media. 2) Your likes: me gusta + one thing or a verb (me gusta bailar), me gustan + several things (me gustan los deportes), me encanta / me encantan for “I love”; to agree, say a mí también, and to agree with a negative, a mí tampoco. 3) Where things are: enfrente de, al lado de, entre, cerca de (de + el = del, a + el = al). 4) Shopping: una libra de, una botella de, medio kilo de, hay muchos. Your task at the end of the lesson: a five-sentence presentation with a time, two likes, a place in your neighborhood and a purchase with its quantity.

titulo.en: Level A1 test

objetivo.en: Show what you have learned in a mini-interview: tell about your weekend, say since when you have lived in Quito and talk about your plans.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Voy al mercado el sábado pasado.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Fui al mercado el sábado pasado.

explicacion.en: El sábado pasado is finished, so the verb must be in the preterite: fui, not the present voy.
Plans use ir + a + infinitive. Do not forget the a: voy a visitar.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Vivo en Quito desde tres meses.

explicacion.en: Desde needs a starting point (septiembre). With an amount of time, use hace: llegué hace tres meses.
Question words always carry a tilde: qué, cómo, dónde, cuándo. Without it, que means “that”.

titulo.en: Sound of the day: stress and the tilde

texto.en: Every Spanish word has one stressed syllable. If a word ends in a vowel, n or s, the stress falls on the second-to-last syllable: casa, hablan, buenos. If it ends in any other consonant, the stress falls on the last syllable: español, hablar. When the stress is somewhere else, a tilde shows it: sábado, inglés, también, está. The tilde also tells apart words that look alike: qué (what) and que (that), está (is) and esta (this). Say them slowly: qué, está, sábado, inglés, también.

titulo.en: The A1 test: a mini-interview

texto.en: In this last class of the level, Sofía interviews you. Be ready to do three things. 1) Tell what you did last weekend: preterite of -ar verbs (visité, caminé, compré), of -er and -ir verbs (comí, salí, volví) and of ir and hacer (fui, hice). 2) Say since when you live somewhere and how long ago you arrived: Vivo en Quito desde septiembre. Llegué hace tres meses. 3) Talk about your plans with ir + a + infinitive: Voy a descansar. Remember the spelling: ¿…? and ¡…! and the tildes (qué, está, sábado, inglés). Good luck!
